episodes.title: I Tried the Best Food in Sydney, Australia!! (Here’s What You Have to Eat)
episodes.description:
This is an ultimate food tour in Sydney, Australia! 

We're going to eat some of the best food, fast food, and diversity of food in Australia. Most importantly I was amazed at the variety and quality of authentic food in Australia. 

A huge thanks to Lily Huynh https://www.youtube.com/@biteswithlily for taking me around, we had a lot of fun eating. 

🇦🇺 Trying the Best Thai Food in Sydney: https://youtu.be/T3Kl15__GYA?si=KFXZUr-kndpZBCB2 
👉 SUBSCRIBE for more: https://www.youtube.com/@MarkWiens   

Here are all the places we visited in this video: 

Raineri's Continental Delicatessen (https://maps.app.goo.gl/VmAeQMiduqa5GMeB7) - This sandwich spot in Sydney is viral and famous for a reason, they have some of the best Italian deli sandwiches you will ever try, and they serve generous portions with very friendly family service. 

Frango Charcoal Chicken (https://maps.app.goo.gl/mQvPpDH6NjG3aWZy9) - This family run fast food chain serves Portuguese style grilled chicken, that’s quality, and extremely tasty. Their legendary sauce is so addictive you won’t be able to stop eating. 

Pho An Bankstown (https://maps.app.goo.gl/t3AtydrXHwaHt62y8) - You can’t visit Sydney without eating some Vietnamese food and Lily said her family always comes here for the best pho in town. 

Al Aseel (https://maps.app.goo.gl/KoQaPEcrfVYZT9pV8) - If you love Lebanese food, Al Aseel is an institution in Sydney, Australia, and their food was fantastic, especially the garlic chicken and kibbeh nayyeh. 

Papa Curry (https://maps.app.goo.gl/mtQG8XsDLaGxQYB96) - Harris Park is known as being a Little India of Sydney, and I was excited to try some Indian food. We started with some pani puri, delicious. 

Dosa Hut (https://maps.app.goo.gl/eJEmS5DSwtpa8FKY7) - And the main event was at Dosa Hut, widely considered one of the top Indian Restaurants in Sydney for dosa and biryani, both of which were highlights. 

Sydney, Australia is multicultural and the food is outstanding.

episodes.description:

Norway has some of the world’s best king crab you will ever taste! And today we’ll be going to the source, a place called Kirkenes, in Northern Norway for a taste of the freshest Norwegian King Crab you can possibly get, plucked directly from the Barents Sea, boiled and steamed, and we’ll taste it directly from the sea! 

A huge thank you to Snowhotel Kirkenes (Snow Resort Kirkenes: https://www.snowresortkirkenes.com/) and Dirk for taking me on this epic King Crab Safari, it was truly a once in a lifetime experience, and without a doubt the best tasting single crab I’ve ever had in my life. 

Fishing - But first Dirk took us fishing in the Barents Sea, we headed out on the boat and got fishing immediately. Along with a bunch of small fish, we managed to catch a small cod fish, which was perfect for dinner.

Crab Safari - The Crab Safari is the highlight, and it’s one of the top reasons you should visit Kirkenes, Norway. You pull the crabs right out of the sea and cook them up moments later in the fisherman hut. Get ready for the best tasting crab of your life! 

Fish Meal - Finally, we headed back to the Snow Resort Kirkenes where the Chef made us an amazing dinner using the cod we caught in the morning. 

Thank you for watching this video and if you love crab, you have to visit Kirkenes in your lifetime!

episodes.title: I Ate the Best $10 Hot Dog in My Life!!
episodes.description:
Today we’re eating a $10 hot dog followed by a $500 meal at one of the most isolated and unique restaurants in Norway! 

Friends in the video: 
Jeffrey Merrihue (https://www.instagram.com/xtremefoodies_/) 
Kevin Chan (https://www.instagram.com/finediningexp/)

Our food adventure all begins in Bergen, where we picked up our rental car… and Bergen happens to have one of the best hot dog stalls in the country. 

Trekroneren, Bergen, Norway (https://maps.app.goo.gl/r3hg5JfDH1XTbT8TA) - This place self proclaimed says they serve the world's best hot dog, and after trying it I have to agree. I tried their signature reindeer sausage, lingonberry, crispy onions - and it was one of the best sausages I’ve ever had. Price - 95 KR ($10.10)

Iris, Salmon Eye, Norway (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Yw8isGiVywxEiThg9) - Next up we drove a couple hours to get to Salmon Eye, and within a beautiful fjord you’ll find one of the most unique dining destinations in the world - Iris!

Our meal started with a trip to the Boat House, before we took the to the largest floating art installation in the world, home to Iris Restaurant. Head Chef Anika Madsen has worked in top kitchen in Denmark before opening Iris, where her and her husband and team now serve an 18 course meal that’s called Expedition Dining. 

Here are all the dishes I tried: 
CONE OF PLENTY - Aromatic herbs, fermented gooseberry and jasmine blossom.
TIDEMARK - Scallop, oyster emulsion, salads from Astrid & lemon butter sauce
500 METERS - Blue mussel, beach crab and rock weed
TOPPTUR - Crispy onion, langoustine tartare and smoked fresh cheese
COAT OF ARMS - Crispy croustade, Gastro Unika Gold caviar & salted mahogany clam
BROWN CRAB CIRCUIT - Toasted blinis, poached brown crab, crispy seaweed, black currant leaf, reindeer mousse & preserved pine cones
IT'S A TRAP! - Shrimp, tomatoes & tamarind
CRACK THE SILENCE - Sea urchin, fresh greens, raspberry & rose hip Nam Jim
WEEDS OF THE SEA - Cuttlefish, celeriac & lovage
NOT YOUR FINNBIFF - Reindeer filet, lardo, pepper sauce and confit fennel
TRASH OR TREASURE? - Scallop offcuts, horseradish, squid ink & lemon rind
SPRUCED UP - Crispy tartelet, pickled spruce needles, pine sorbet & caviar
WHEY HIT WONDER - Fresh Brunost, laminated brioche, red currant, strawberries & rum/plum ice cream

Price - 4,700 NOK ($473.84) per person (with wine over $500 per person)

Both the $10 hot dog and the $500 meal at Iris were absolutely incredible experiences.

Singapore has some of the world’s best street food, and today we’re not only eating 10 of the best Singapore street foods, but we’re going to be ranking them! 

Disclaimer: I would like to emphasize that the ranking is about the dish, rather than the restaurant, and all 10 of the dishes featured are some of the best in Singapore that you have to try. 

Kaya Toast at Ah Seng (Hai Nam) Coffee (https://maps.app.goo.gl/w3nrAGijrxW5mD3n6) - We’re starting things off with kaya toast, the most iconic Singaporean breakfast. Price - $5.20 SGD for everything

Chicken Rice at Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice (https://maps.app.goo.gl/HaxUzgFBVeyVFd2U9) - Probably the most famous of all Singapore street food dishes in chicken rice, and I headed to Tiong Bahru to try it. Price - $4.80 SGD

Char Kway Teow at Meng Kee Fried Kway Teow (https://maps.app.goo.gl/ioTmt6e7STtWsPNk6) - Singaporeans are extremely passionate about char kway teow, and I went to Havelock Road Cooked Food Centre to try a local version. Price - $5 SGD

Bak Chor Mee at No. 25 Minced Meat Noodle (https://maps.app.goo.gl/yhCkunKBwKpMSNbp9) - Known as BCM, bak chor mee is a favorite Singapore hawker noodle dish. Price - $6.50 SGD

Bak Kut Teh at Ya Hua Bak Kut Teh (https://maps.app.goo.gl/aNLx7HWzrNMcT4WC6) - The broth is the best part of bak kut teh, that white pepper makes all the difference. Price - $14.80 for the prime ribs 

Roti Prata at Jom Makan (https://maps.app.goo.gl/MNBNoTgqNB67aCA38) - Tucked within the Tekka Centre of Singapore, don’t miss their roti prata and especially their flooded prata. Price - $2.20 SGD for the plain prata 

Nasi Lemak at Spicy Wife Nasi Lemak (https://maps.app.goo.gl/ZE8pfECgzRRAvvA29) - This nasi lemak is famous for their huge piece of fried chicken, and I’m a huge fan of nasi lemak! Price - $6.50 SGD

Katong Laksa at Famous Sungei Road Trishaw Laksa (https://maps.app.goo.gl/iitBqbmjyZZzsTto8) - Next up on our Singapore street food tour, we’re at the always busy Hong Lim Complex to eat laksa. Price - $12 SGD

Satay at 168 CMY Satay (https://maps.app.goo.gl/xivy1MXEDgyFHSJw7) - This satay stall located within Chinatown Complex was featured in the Michelin Guide. Price - $8 SGD 

Oyster Omelet at Hup Kee Fried Oyster Omelette (https://maps.app.goo.gl/TyykdwymWrEUF9EXA) - Next up we’re heading to the iconic Newton Food Centre to eat a classic oyster omelette. Price - $8 SGD

And that’s 10 of the best Singapore street foods you have to try when you’re in Singapore. What is your favorite?

Dongjin Restaurant (동진식당 동문시장점 https://maps.app.goo.gl/bw4NDmwiW41H5JyCA) - We’re heading to the Dongmun Market to try another Korean food you have to eat in Jeju - Jeju Pork Noodles (Gogiguksu / 고기국수), and I also tried the Spicy Noodles (Bibim-guksu / 비빔국수). Price - 8,000 KRW ($5.49) per bowl  

Jina Tteokjip (진아떡집) - As a bonus, when you’re at the market don’t miss Omegi-tteok (오메기떡)

Golmok Sikdang (골목식당 https://maps.app.goo.gl/23j7yEJLaK3WnbBY9) - This local Korean restaurant at the back of the market serves pheasant bbq and Buckwheat Pheasant Noodles (Kkwong Maemil Kalguksu / 꿩메밀칼국수), and it was one of my favorite meals in Jeju. Price - 43,000 KRW ($29.53) for everything 

Jakjedo BBQ (작제도 흑돼지 장작구이 https://maps.app.goo.gl/6DMH9VrwqsubJRg7A) - This restaurant is a hidden gem of Jeju Korean black pork bbq, must eat when you’re in Jeju. Jeju Black Pork (Heuk-dwaeji / 흑돼지). Price - 76,000 KRW ($52.20) for everything 

Don’t miss the amazing Korean food in Jeju!

Go Halmang-ne (고할망네), Andeok-myeon, Jeju Island (https://maps.app.goo.gl/2RaJoCosQfzQfxEX9) - Continuing with our Korean seafood tour in Jeju I had to try my favorite Korean food of all time Spicy Braised Hairtail Fish (Galchi Jorim / 갈치조림). Price - 46,000 KRW ($31.59) total

Christbel - Next up in Soweto we tried a different type of kota, this one a Kota Mince. 

Fried Liver Stall - Soweto has some amazing food spots, and we then headed to a man who’s been selling Ox Heart and Liver for 15 years.

B n G Taste Fast Food - Probably the most famous of all South African food is Shisanyama, grilled meat, and South Africa really knows how to do it. We had a full mix of meats including beef, chicken, and boerewors.  

But which South African street food of the day was my favorite?

episodes.title: I Ate Extreme Indian Food in South Africa!! (Bunny Chow)
episodes.description:
🇿🇦 Best South African Fast Food: https://youtu.be/HUcfNu5wED8
👉 SUBSCRIBE for more: https://www.youtube.com/@MarkWiens

Today we’re eating some of the best food in Durban, South Africa for bunny chow and shisanyama.

Durban is a city that’s home to the Zulu People and one of the biggest Indian ethnic populations of any city outside of India. One of the ultimate South African foods you have to try in Durban is called Bunny Chow, an Indian South African food invented in Durban, and we’re about to try two different versions and find out why it’s one of the greatest dishes ever. 

Here are the places we ate at in Durban, South Africa:

Patel Vegetarian Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/PUPiDuFXp9zhbC3u9) - Open since 1911, this place is an institution and they serve some of the best bunny chows in Durban. 

Mojo’s Car Wash and Shisanyama (https://maps.app.goo.gl/C97sK2biK1rpPogU9) - Along with bunny chow, you can’t visit Durban without eating Shisanyama and we headed to this spot in Mayville Township for all the meats. 

Gounden’s Restaurant (https://maps.app.goo.gl/fa6PHAJVYWCZs5te6) - But the top recommendation for where to eat the best bunny chow was hand down Gounden’s Restaurant for their Mutton Bunny Chow and I was not going to miss it. 

Skipper’s Fish and Chips (https://maps.app.goo.gl/LmiKwzq1HmK9CdEY8) - We finished the day with a legendary fish and chips shop near the beach.

Durban is an amazing city with a mix of cultures and foods. It was another extremely delicious day in South Africa!

Thank you to Gumbo and Makhosi from https://experientialtravelafrica.com/ for helping me to arrange this trip to South Africa.

episodes.description:
🇿🇦 I Tried South Africa's Bunny Chow: https://youtu.be/KbduZVDxlRg 
👉 SUBSCRIBE for more: https://www.youtube.com/@MarkWiens

Today we’re going on an ultimate South African food tour in Cape Town, South Africa where we’ll eat the best gatsby and find out what Cape Malay food really is! 

Super Fisheries - We’re starting this Cape Town food tour today in Athlone to try the original Gatsby, a giant fast food creation that is one of the most well known street foods in Cape Town and this is where they invented it. I enjoyed their amazing Calamari, Fish and Chips Gatsby. Price - 180 ZAR ($10.72)

Arshad's Kitchen - Next up we’re heading to Arshad's Kitchen to try some of the best chicken tikka in Cape Town, and they serve amazing Halal grilled food. Price - 60 ZAR ($3.57)

The Golden Dish - But nothing in Cape Town will prepare you for the shock and amazing gatsby sandwiches that you can order at the Golden Dish. I tried their insane Masala Steak Full House Gatsby which is the king of South African food and one of the world’s best sandwiches! Price - 260 ZAR ($15.49) 

Fish On The Rocks - Cape Town is also very well known for their fish and chips and Fish On The Rocks in Hout Bay is extremely iconic. I tried their Snoek & Chips, Hake & Chips, and their Peri Peri Prawns. Price - 115 ZAR ($6.85) per plate 

Bo-Kaap Kombuis Restaurant - Cape Malay’s are predominantly Muslims that were indentured laborers and enslaved who were brought to the Cape in South Africa, and they developed their own unique food and culture. Cape Malay food is something you have to try in Cape Town. We tried their Boboti, Fish Curry, Prawn Curry, Lamb Curry, Denning Vleis-Lamb, Tomato Bredie Beef, Frikkadel and more!

Thank you to Gumbo and Caleb from https://experientialtravelafrica.com/ for helping me to arrange this trip to South Africa.

episodes.title: Showing ANOTHER Side of Iraq!! (Street Food in Baghdad) 🇮🇶
episodes.description:
🇮🇶 Iraqi Street Food Pt 2: https://youtu.be/Hxw1WI_vuLU
👉 SUBSCRIBE for more: https://www.youtube.com/@MarkWiens

Welcome to Baghdad, Iraq! Today we’re eating the best Iraqi street food in Baghdad! 

A huge thank you to Ahmet and Aya from https://enliltravels.com/ for arranging my trip to Iraq.

Kubba Saray - We’re starting in Old Baghdad to try a unique version of kubba from an old shop tucked within the book and school market. 

Shabandar Café - Located on the iconic Mutanabbi Street in Baghdad, you’ll find the oldest teahouse. And I tried Nooma Basri, a dried lime tea. Afterwards, just outside I ate some classic winter Iraqi street foods including chickpeas and turnips. 

Bourek Taha - Just down the road you’ll find Bourek Taha that has served the Iraqi version of bourek for generations. 

Mr. Garbage Raisin Juice - This place is legendary and their raisin juice hits the spot. 

Abu Hussein Iraqi Gus - Just about every country in the Middle East has their own version of shawarma, and every version is a little different. Gus is the Iraqi version of shawarma, and I was very curious to see how it tasted. 

Al Qameh Restaurant - For lunch in Baghdad, Ahemet took me to one of his favorite spots for a mix of homestyle Iraqi dishes and stews including lamb quzi. 

Baghdadi Restaurant - But of all the amazing Iraqi foods, Masgouf is the king of them all, a slow roasted freshwater carp fish, standing vertically with a blazing fire. This is one of the world’s greatest fire grilling bbq techniques. 

Hamooqy - Finally, we headed to Hamooqy, a legendary Iraqi street food vendor to try his unique meatballs and omelets.

episodes.title: Winter Olympics Food Tour - 24 Hours in Italy!!
episodes.description:
What’s it like to spend 24 hours at the Winter Olympics? And how’s the food? Thank you to The @Olympics and @YouTube for inviting me to the Winter Olympics - Milano Cortina 2026! 

I traveled to Milan, then took a 4.5 hour van ride into the beautiful mountains of Livigno in the Italian Alps for the Games. 

In this video I’ll show you what it’s like to spend a full day at the Winter Olympics in Livigno, starting with morning wakeup, breakfast, and a quick room tour. We also got an exclusive behind the scenes tour to the top of the big air ski jump for the view. I’ll show you all the food I ate for lunch at the Olympic Hospitality. 

Another highlight was getting to chat with Pat Burgener, a professional snowboarder and musician at the Olympics - and it was cool to hear his response to “what an Olympic athlete eats?” 

Finally, you can’t come to Italy without trying some of the local traditional Italian food, and I was excited to try Pizzoccheri, Tzigoiner, and Salmì di cervo. An amazing meal! 

It was an incredible day at the Winter Olympics 2026! 

Thank you again to The Olympics and YouTube. #MilanoCortina2026 #invitedbyyoutube

9 AM Sajad Abo Oruk - Just down the road we headed to the next spot, a Baghdad street food stall specializing in a different type of Iraqi breakfast. We tried Bagela bil Dihin - Fava beans and fat, and Makhlama - Iraqi omelet.

4 PM Haidar Double Falafel - How is Iraqi falafel? We’re about to find out by going to try the best Iraqi falafel in Baghdad. 

5 PM al-Tahrir Square, Baghdad, Iraq

8 PM Maslawi Pacha - Another incredible Iraqi dish is known as Pacha - sheep head and organs, and the fried mumbar - intestines stuffed with rice - was on another level!

episodes.description:
Watch the full @NatGeo series: https://youtu.be/CE6Y8tqhO4A?si=SnzmFzCmEcr5x57C 

Today we’re exploring Iraqi Kurdistan and the incredible city of Erbil! It’s a city with thousands of years of history that all surround the ancient citadel in the center of the city. 

Machko Cafe - We’re starting with breakfast at this amazing and historical cafe for the full Kurdish breakfast including lots of tea. 

Yassin Kebab - If there’s one place you have to eat kebabs when you’re in Erbil, it must be Yassin Kebab, loved by both locals and visitors, and known for serving some of the best kebabs in Iraq.

episodes.title: Insane Old Delhi Street Food!! (Best Indian Food Ever)
episodes.description:
It’s Ramadan, and tonight we’re going on an Indian street food tour in Old Delhi. But first, we’re having Iftar (evening meal breaking the fast) at Jama Masjid in the heart of Old Delhi! Huge thank you to Anubhav Sapra @delhifoodwalks for arranging this amazing tour! 

Jama Masjid - We’re starting at Jama Masjid where every evening during Ramadan over 30,000 people gather for Iftar, which is the meal after sunset during Ramadan. It was a beautiful moment, sitting together with 30,000 people sharing dates, fruits, samosas, and pakoras. 

Qureshi Kabab Corner - After Jama Masjid, we hit the streets of Old Delhi, an Indian street food paradise. First up for some of the best seekh kebabs at Qureshi Kabab Corner. 

Karim Hotel - You can’t go on a food tour to Old Delhi without paying tribute to Karim Hotel, an institution. And Anubhav and I tried Chicken Burra, Brain Curry, Mutton Korma, and Chicken Ishtoo.

Aslam Chicken - For one of the world’s most buttery butter chicken you have to go to Aslam. They grill their chicken, then drench it in yoghurt and cream, sprinkle it with masala, and submerge it in melted butter.

Haji Mohd. Hussain - This is one of the most legendary places to eat in Old Delhi, and their fried chicken is triple fried to give it insane crispiness, sprinkled in masala, and served with a tangy chutney. 

Taufiq Biryani - Next up on our Indian street food tour we tried Delhi Biryani, my first time to try this style. It was all about the pickle achar that gave it so much flavor. 

Meetha Samosa - Finally, another Ramadan sweet snack is a sweet samosa filled with mild solids. 

Ramadan is a special time in Old Delhi, and Iftar at Jama Masjid along with extreme Indian street food in Old Delhi was an incredible experience!

episodes.title: London’s Oldest Restaurants - We DID NOT Expect This!
episodes.description:
We're trying the oldest restaurants in London — from a 1900 East End cafe all the way back to London's oldest restaurant, open since 1798. Thanks to @GaryEats for joining me!

We're eating the signature dish at each one, traveling further back in time with every stop: a full English breakfast, my first ever coronation chicken sandwich, London's original fast food, a legendary seafood spot that only opens for 3 hours a day, and finally the oldest restaurant in London!

The big question: are these historic London restaurants surviving on their history, or do they still serve delicious food? Let's find out.

episodes.title: Afghanistan is DANGEROUS for Food Lovers!! 🇦🇫 (Kabul's Best Street Food)
episodes.description:
Today we're going on an ultimate Afghanistan street food tour in Kabul! Kabul is the biggest, liveliest, and most surprising city in Afghanistan, and today we’re exploring a side of this country that most people outside rarely get to see—incredible food, ancient traditions, and mind-blowing hospitality. 

Today, our local friend Bilal (https://www.instagram.com/bilalkwardak ) along with my friend Jon (🎥 https://www.instagram.com/jontravelist/ ), are going deep into the heart of the Kabul for a full-day street food marathon. We start our morning with rich, creamy Qaymaq (Afghan clotted cream) before diving into Kabul's busiest street markets for handmade cheese, steamed Mantu dumplings, and comforting Aush noodles. 

We'll also wander through Ka Faroshi, Kabul's famous 200-year-old bird market, grab some street-side liver and tripe, and taste Chainaki—a classic lamb and chickpea stew slow-cooked inside ceramic teapots. 

After washing it down with fresh pomegranate juice and crispy stuffed Bolani flatbread, we finish the night at Super Shinwari for an epic feast of Shinwari White Lamb Karahi and melt-in-your-mouth Dampokht lamb.

episodes.title: Inside Afghanistan's MEAT Paradise!! (Unreal Afghan Food)
episodes.description:
Afghan food is a meat lover's paradise — from a legendary slow-simmered breakfast in Kabul Old City to a riverside lamb feast in Paghman Valley, just 45 minutes from the city at the base of the Hindu Kush mountains!

Afghanistan's meat obsession is real, and today my friend Bilal Kamal and I are experiencing it from morning to night. We start in Kabul Old City with kalla pacha at Faizi Kalla wa Pacha Restaurant — slow-simmered sheep's head and trotters that just might be one of the world's greatest breakfasts. Next, hot out of the tandoor oven, we eat samsa — flaky Afghan baked meat pies — at Samarqand Sambosa Tandoori. Then we drive to the base of the Hindu Kush mountains to Paghman Valley, where locals escape the city for rivers, fresh fruit, lush green trees, and incredible food. Sitting riverside at Hamesha Bahar, we finish with rosh — fall-apart lamb stew cooked with potatoes and onions — for the ultimate Afghan countryside feast!

Today we're going completely off grid in Afghanistan — two hours from Kabul, deep into the mountains of Wardak, to my friend Bilal Kamal's home village, where he's taking me to meet the elders — his father and uncles — and cook a traditional Afghan feast together. episodes.description:
Pampanga is the culinary capital of the Philippines — and today we're eating the most iconic Kapampangan food all in one day, from the birthplace of the original sizzling sisig to crispy lechon kawali. And we're in good hands: Pampanga native Paul Chez of @TeamCanlasTV is showing us his hometown's most legendary spots!

We start with Kapampangan home-cooking classics at Batcha-batchang Lutong Ulam — beef lengua, lechon kawali, sipo egg, and pork binagoongan — then feast on Pampanga's goat obsession at Taldawa Kambingan Grill: goat sinigang, kilawin, papaitan, and kaldereta. Then it's time for history: Aling Lucing, the restaurant by the railroad tracks in Angeles City where sizzling sisig was invented. episodes.title: The Philippines Most EXTREME Food in Pampanga!! 🇵🇭
episodes.description:
We're eating extreme Filipino food in Pampanga, Philippines 🇵🇭 — stuffed frogs (betute tugak), mole crickets (kamaru), fermented rice (buro), and adobong balut, plus heirloom Kapampangan food from Atching Lillian, the guardian of Kapampangan cuisine. With Paul Chez @TeamCanlasTV

This is Day 2 in Pampanga, and this time we're in San Fernando on a mission to eat the most extreme Filipino food in the country! We start easy at LBS Bakeshop & Kitchenette, a three-generation panaderia that bakes 8,000 cheese breads a day, with pancit palabok and dinuguan for breakfast. Then straight across the street into the San Fernando Public Market for burong Kapampangan at Lola Denang Canteen — fermented rice with shrimp and fish, the dish that divides Filipinos. From there it's Cely's Carinderia, a legendary turo-turo since the 1970s, for betute tugak (stuffed frogs), kamaru (adobo mole crickets), pulutok (minced pork lungs), lagat puso (banana blossom), and adobong balut — including one dish I was scared to try. We finish in the town of Mexico at Kusinang Matua, the ancestral home of Atching Lillian Borromeo, Filipino food historian and the guardian of Kapampangan cuisine, cooking heirloom recipes in a 200-year-old kitchen to answer one question: why is Pampanga the culinary capital of the Philippines?

episodes.title: Why Montreal Is Canada's BEST Food City!! (Smoked Meat, Bagels & Poutine)
episodes.description:
Montreal food tour — We're eating 100 years of the Canada's most legendary food in one day with Luke Martin of @LukeMartin including the bagel debate that began in 1919, Schwartz's smoked meat since 1928, a sandwich with rules you can't break since 1932, and real old-school Quebec poutine!

Some call Montreal the best food city in Canada — and today we're going to find out why? 

We start in Mile End with the great Montreal bagel debate: St-Viateur Bagel (since 1957) versus Fairmount Bagel (since 1919), the family that started it all. Then the dish Quebec was built on — fèves au lard, beans, lard, and maple, unchanged since 1938 at La Binerie Mont-Royal. Next, the Wilensky's Special at Wilensky's Light Lunch, a sandwich with strict rules since 1932, then the most famous deli in Canada: Schwartz's, where smoked meat is cured ten days, smoked every morning, and hand-carved exactly as it was in 1928. And we finish with the original old-school Quebec poutine at a tiny 1958 diner that still brews its own spruce beer!

episodes.title: Is Canada's Fast Food BETTER Than America? 🇨🇦
episodes.description:
Montreal has the best fast food in all of Canada 🇨🇦 — and today we're eating a 70-year secret sauce burger, steamé hot dogs since 1912, a drive-in inside a giant orange, and the chicken and chouriço poutine locals call one of the best dishes in the city. With Luke Martin @LukeMartin 

Day 2 in Montreal, and today it's all about casse-croûte — Montreal's own fast food universe, fast, cheap, and found nowhere else on Earth! Luke Martin of Chopsticks Travel is back, and we start with the new legend: Ma Poule Mouillée in the Plateau for piri-piri chicken and their famous chicken, chouriço and São Jorge cheese poutine. Then back to 1912 at Montreal Pool Room on the Main for the original steamé hot dog, before the other side of the debate — the toasté — at Decarie Hot Dog in Ville Saint-Laurent, open since 1969. We pull into Gibeau Orange Julep, the three-storey orange on Décarie Boulevard serving its secret Julep since 1932, then head to Montréal-Nord for Dic Ann's, where one family has guarded a burger sauce recipe since 1954. And we finish in Saint-Henri at Greenspot, a 1947 diner where you can order every Montreal fast food ever invented on one table — smoked meat, poutine, steamés, and more!

episodes.title: Food is WILD on the World’s Biggest Island!!
episodes.description:
Welcome to Greenland 🇬🇱 Let's try Greenlandic Food!
Airalo eSIM for your next trip: https://try.airalo.com/MARK — use code MARK for a discount. This video is sponsored by Airalo.

In this video we take a boat deep into Nuuk Fjord, catch our own lunch, and eat it at Qooqqut Nuan, a restaurant at the edge of the world, then finish with a Greenlandic barbecue on the beach: whale, seal, and Arctic ingredients cooked on hot rocks. 

Welcome to Greenland, where every meal is an unknown adventure and whatever you catch is what you eat! Day one in Nuuk, and we're heading an hour by boat through Nuuk Fjord — past icebergs we pull up for drinking water — fishing for redfish and cod along the way. The catch goes straight to Qooqqut Nuan, a tiny summer-only restaurant on a hill at Qooqqut, in the middle of nowhere, where the kitchen turns your own fish into lunch, and I couldn't believe what they served! Then back in Nuuk, as the sun goes down, we've arranged a traditional Greenlandic barbecue on the beach at Inuk Hostels, looking out over the fjord: whale and seal grilled on hot rocks, Greenlandic snacks, a song, and one thing I've never tried in my life. This is Greenland food, straight from the Arctic!

episodes.title: Surviving GREENLAND!! Arctic Food for 4,500 Years!!
episodes.description:
Traditional Greenlandic food in Nuuk, Greenland — invited on a local Inuit seal hunt, a seal BBQ on the rocks, and Chef Aggu Broberg cooking suaasat, the national dish of Greenland!

In this video we’re eating real, authentic Greenlandic food the way it’s been eaten for thousands of years. It starts in the Nuuk Fjord, where a local Inuit hunter invited us along on his traditional seal hunt — legal, regulated, and still the foundation of how Greenland feeds itself in a land where almost nothing grows. Right there on the rocks we had a Greenlandic hot rock BBQ with fresh seal meat (and a taste of raw seal liver, hunter style). Then we brought the seal back to Nuuk, picked up fresh fish and reindeer, and handed everything to Chef Aggu Broberg of Restaurant Sarfalik, who cooked us a full Greenlandic meal — fish, seal, a reindeer finale, and suaasat, the national dish of Greenland: seal soup with rice and onions. Nothing is wasted, everything is wild, and this is Greenlandic food at its most real!

▶️ Watch the full Greenland food series: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLc1k8XCPvFTw

episodes.title: I Tried the World’s Most UNUSUAL Buffet!! (in Greenland 🇬🇱)
episodes.description:
What’s it like to eat at a buffet in Greenland? 🇬🇱 
Today we’re eating 25 dishes of traditional Greenlandic food at our hotel, Hotel Hans Egede in Nuuk — raw, cured and dried Arctic seafood, wild game, hot Greenlandic mains, dessert, and one final surprise from Chef Aggu Broberg. 

I’ve been eating buffets all over the world for twenty years, and I’ve never seen anything like this one. We’re staying at Hotel Hans Egede in the heart of Nuuk, and upstairs at Sarfalik, Chef Aggu Broberg has laid out a buffet of 25 Greenlandic dishes — and absolutely nothing on it is farmed or raised. Everything is wild, straight from the Arctic. So we set ourselves a challenge: eat every single dish. Round one is the cold table, fourteen dishes, raw, cured and dried, where the real Greenland lives. Round two is the hot Arctic mains. Then a question I couldn’t answer before this trip — what does the Arctic do for dessert? And Chef Aggu saved one last thing for the end, a proper Greenlandic goodbye infused with Arctic herbs. Twenty-five dishes, one night, and half of them you won’t find anywhere else on Earth!

episodes.title: Indians Kept Telling Me to Eat HERE!! (Lucknow Food Tour)
episodes.description:
The ultimate Lucknow food tour — today we’re eating the best Indian food in Lucknow in one day: kulcha nihari, sheermal, galouti kebab burger, Lucknowi biryani, and chicken masala!

Lucknow might be the greatest food city in India the world still hasn’t discovered. For 250 years it was the capital of royal Awadhi cooking, and today we’re eating our way through five legendary spots in one day. We start at Raheem’s at Akbari Gate in Chowk with one of the world’s great breakfasts: kulcha nihari, slow-cooked mutton with the softest bread in India. Then down Sheermal Wali Gali to Ali Hussain Sheermal, where one family has baked the saffron-and-milk flatbread for around 200 years. At Kareem Kababi in Aminabad we eat melt-in-your-mouth galouti kebabs, boti kebab paratha rolls, and Lucknow’s own kebab burger. Next, a rickshaw race to Lalla Biryani in Chowk for the Lucknowi biryani that sells out within hours. And finally, dinner at Dastarkhwan in Kaiserbagh: shami kebab, mutton rogan josh, and the chicken masala I’d been dreaming about all day — cooked on a giant tawa. This is Day 1 of our 3-day Lucknow, India food tour!

7:03 Sheermal on Sheermal Wali Gali
10:54 Galouti Kebabs & Kebab Burger at Kareem Kababi, Aminabad
